prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2015 — summary (under 500 words)

Core vision: Stronger economy, fairer society, opportunity for everyone. Finish balancing the budget fairly; invest for a high-skill, low‑carbon UK; protect rights and the environment; spread opportunity from early years to retirement.

Economy and jobs
- Balance the structural current budget by 2017/18; debt falling year-on-year; allow borrowing for productive investment.
- Fair taxes: raise Personal Allowance to £12,500; clamp down on avoidance; levy on high-value properties; no rises in Income Tax, NI, VAT or Corporation Tax rates.
- Industrial strategy: double economy-wide innovation spend; protect and grow science funding; expand Catapults; support advanced manufacturing, green tech, digital and creative sectors.
- Banking reform and competition; expand British Business Bank; back alternative finance and community banking.
- Infrastructure: HS2 as part of high-speed network, major rail electrification, North and SW upgrades, East–West Rail; cautious airports policy with no net runway increase.
- Tech: near-universal high-speed broadband (99.9%); scale-up support; STEM and coding; digital-by-default public services.

Energy, climate and environment
- Five Green Laws: Nature, Zero Carbon Britain, Green Transport, Resource Efficiency & Zero Waste, Green Buildings.
- Power sector 2030 decarbonisation target; 60% renewables by 2030; end unabated coal by 2025; expand Green Investment Bank and community energy.
- Air quality plan with Low Emission Zones; ultra-low emission vehicle shift by 2040; cycling investment.
- Resource efficiency: 70% recycling target; circular economy; stronger green procurement.
- Nature: statutory Natural Capital targets; new National Nature Parks; plant a tree per child; complete coastal path.

Tax, welfare, work and consumers
- Universal Credit rollout with fairer sanctions; 1% cap on working-age benefit uprating until 2017/18; protect disability/parental leave benefits.
- Childcare: towards 20 hours free for ages 2–4 and from end of paid leave; Tax-Free Childcare; 85% childcare support in UC.
- Work: expand Shared Parental Leave; transparency on gender pay and low pay; Living Wage in central government; fairer zero-hours rules.
- Pensions: triple lock in law; single-tier pension; auto-enrolment completion; explore single-rate tax relief.
- Consumers: 24-hour energy switching; smart meters; rail fares capped at inflation overall; curb payday lenders and FOBTs.

Education and skills
- Protect funding from early years to 19; Pupil Premium retained.
- End child illiteracy/innumeracy by 2025; qualified teachers in every class; funded CPD; slim core curriculum incl. PSHE, consent, RE.
- Stronger local accountability; admissions fairness; extend free school meals to all primary.
- Double employers hiring apprentices; more higher apprenticeships; FE/6th form fairness; widen HE participation and review finance.

Health and care
- At least £8bn extra for NHS England by 2020; integrate health and social care with pooled budgets by 2018.
- Mental health parity: £500m a year more; access/waiting time standards; crisis care; children’s services transformation.
- Public health: smoking measures, alcohol minimum pricing (subject to legal outcome), food labelling, active travel.
- Social care: implement cap on care costs; improve care workforce standards; £250 Carer’s Bonus; carers’ leave consultation.

Homes
- Build 300,000 homes a year; at least 10 Garden Cities; brownfield first; Housing Investment Bank; planning reform with stronger local plans.
- Affordable options: Affordable Rent, Shared Ownership, Rent to Own; more council/HA flexibility.
- Private renting: multi‑year tenancies with predictable increases; licensing powers; ban excessive letting fees; deposit loans for under‑30s.
- Greener homes: aim Band C for all by 2035 (fuel-poor and rented by 2027); council tax rebate for insulation.

Rights, policing, drugs and immigration
- Protect Human Rights Act; Digital Bill of Rights; oppose mass surveillance; new Freedoms Act.
- Equality: action on gender pay, BAME disparities, disability access, LGBT+ rights.
- Replace Police & Crime Commissioners with Police Boards; Victims’ Bill of Rights; tackle VAWG; rehabilitation focus, presumption against short short-term sentences.
- Drugs: Portugal-style diversion for possession; no jail for personal possession; medicinal cannabis.
- Borders: complete entry/exit checks; faster asylum; students out of migration target stats; fair enforcement.

Devolution and democracy
- Votes at 16; STV for Commons and local elections; elected Lords; £10k cap on donations; constitutional convention; Home Rule for nations; English devolution on demand; retain Barnett (with fair Welsh floor).

International
- Pro‑EU with reform; referendum only on future treaty power transfers; back TTIP with NHS and standards safeguarded.
- Single Security Budget; SDSR; end continuous nuclear patrols; NATO/EU defence cooperation.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; lead on climate deal, tax transparency, human rights and LGBT+ rights abroad.
